title: Recommendations to Grow Algal Culture
author: Roscoff Culture Collection
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s2qegdw
materials: Please make sure that your laboratory has suitable equipment and conditions for the reception and maintenance of the cultures. Every culture in the RCC catalogue has a detailed form on our website ( http://roscoff-culture-collection.org/ ), where you will find a range of information concerning culture conditions for the strain in question (temperature, medium, light intensity, etc.).

steps.title: Prepare Culture Media
steps.instruction: Prepare the defined medium specific to the culture using sterile seawater or artificial seawater.

substeps.instruction: If using natural seawater: use seawater collected off Roscoff (salinity ca. 33 ‰), stored for at least two months in darkness, filtered through 0.22µM filters (Millipore filter GSWPO9000 plus Millipore prefilter AP1507500), and autoclaved.
If using artificial seawater: use salt mixtures as specified on the RCC website (Red Sea Salt is recommended for some cyanobacteria).
Add sterile (autoclaved and/or 0.22µM filtered) nutrient and trace metal stocks to the sterile seawater under a laminar flow hood.
Sterilize vitamins via 0.22µM filtration and store at -20°C; do not autoclave vitamins.

steps.title: Set Up Growth Environment
steps.instruction: Configure the culture room or cabinet with the required light and temperature settings.

substeps.instruction: Set a 12H/12H day/night light cycle using 'daylight' neon tubes (Tabur-Neons Sylvania Daylight F58W/54/765 ref: 0001440 + starter ref: 00007698476).
Maintain light intensity below 100 µEinsteins.m-2.s-1; use a blue filter (« Moonlight Blue 183 » - Minet Eclairages Scéniques) for cultures preferring blue light (e.g., certain cyanobacteria).
Set temperature based on strain type: Polar strains at 4°C, Temperate strains at 15°C, and Tropical strains at 22°C.

steps.title: Prepare Culture Vessels
steps.instruction: Select appropriate sterile containers for the strains.

substeps.instruction: Use single-use sterile polystyrene flasks with ventilated filter caps (Sarstedt ref 831810.002 or Nunc ref 136196), single-use sterile polystyrene tubes (CML ref TCU12PS25), or Erlenmeyers/glass flasks.

steps.title: Receive and Acclimatize Cultures
steps.instruction: Handle the arrival of cultures to minimize transport stress.

substeps.instruction: Store arriving packages at room temperature; do not store in a cold room or freezer.
Transfer flasks into the culture room or cabinet with appropriate temperature and light conditions.
Wait one to two days before transferring cultures into fresh medium to allow recovery from transport stress.

steps.title: Maintain and Monitor Cultures
steps.instruction: Perform regular monitoring and periodic transfers to maintain strain health.

substeps.instruction: Monitor growth daily using direct microscopy, epifluorescence inverted microscopy (for small cells like Prochlorococcus), or flow cytometry.
Transfer most strains every 2-3 weeks using a 1/10 to 1/50 dilution in new medium.

steps.title: Propagate Virus-Host Pairs
steps.instruction: Follow specific procedures for the propagation of viral strains using host microalgal cultures.

substeps.instruction: Store the virus flask at 4°C in darkness upon delivery.
Transfer the host microalgal culture to the incubator and dilute 1/10 – 1/50 (vol/vol) into fresh medium; incubate for 3 to 4 days to reach exponential phase.
Inoculate the host with the viral suspension at a virus:host ratio of 1:10 – 1:50 (vol/vol) and incubate under host growing conditions.
Use a non-infected host culture aliquot as a control to monitor cell lysis (detected by complete clearing of the culture, usually 3 – 7 days post-inoculation).
Store the resulting lysate at 4°C or transfer it immediately; do not keep lysate under host growing conditions for extended periods to avoid resistant hosts.
Optional: Filter lysate through 0.2 µm PES, PC, or GF filters (avoid cellulose acetate) to remove debris.
Store viral suspensions at 4°C for 3 – 4 months, protecting them from intense light, UV, and heat.
